label: Beads
hints: `bd` is the bead store underneath Beadhive: issues chained together with first-class dependencies. Prefer the `bh work` verbs for anything in a bead's lifecycle — reach for `bd` directly only for reads and for fields `bh` does not wrap.
Useful read-only verbs: `bd list`, `bd show <id>`, `bd ready`, `bd search <text>`, `bd query`, `bd status`, `bd children <id>`, `bd history <id>`, `bd gate list`.
Dependencies are the point: `bd dep tree <id>` and `bd blocked` explain why a bead is not ready. A bead is ready only when every dependency is closed and no gate blocks it.
Gates are async wait conditions. A `human` gate closes only by explicit resolution — that is the human-in-the-loop mechanism, not an obstacle to route around.
Record findings as you go with `bd note <id>` and `bd comment <id>`; they are durable and cheap.

approvals.reason: Destroys beads and rewrites references to them. Work is closed or abandoned through the lifecycle, never deleted.
Closes an async gate. Human gates exist precisely to hold work until a person decides; resolving one is that person's call.
Closing a bead directly bypasses the review-and-merge lifecycle that `bh work` enforces.
The merge slot serializes integration across the hive. Taking or releasing it out of band breaks that serialization.
Reverts other workers' in_progress beads on the assumption their lease is stale — it can yank live work away.
